channel.description: Travel reporting, cultural heritage, and responsible exploration worldwide.

item.title: Kuganha Brings Private In-Suite Wellness to the Western Cape Safari
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Kuganha has opened in South Africa’s Western Cape, introducing a new take on the luxury safari experience within a 10,000-hectare rewilded Big Five conservancy less than two and a half hours from Cape Town. Limited to just 10 private tented suites, each measuring at least 320 square metres, the property combines safari, conservation and an unusually comprehensive approach to private wellness, with the entire experience designed around each guest’s own pace.

Wellness is built directly into the suites, rather than confined to a traditional spa. Guests have access to private saunas, steam rooms, a Himalayan salt oxygen halotherapy room, flotation deprivation pods, ice plunge baths, jacuzzi plunge pools and double massage beds, along with an introductory wellness journey to guide them through the facilities. The culinary program follows the same personalized philosophy, with fresh, organic and locally sourced ingredients tailored around each guest’s wellness journey. Meals can be enjoyed privately or at the Kuganha restaurant overlooking the infinity pool, waterhole and surrounding Karoo landscape. Beyond the suites, the property’s rewilding story adds another dimension, with Big Five wildlife reintroduced to land where many species had disappeared centuries ago.

The Curated Take

Kuganha is tapping into an intriguing evolution in luxury wellness: the desire to retreat from the world without giving up the comforts, privacy or personalization of a high-end stay. Here, wellness is not a schedule of treatments guests move through during the day. It is embedded in the accommodation itself, then paired with wildlife, open landscapes and conservation. The result is a safari experience where the natural environment is not simply the backdrop, but part of the restorative proposition.

item.title: Four Seasons Bali Turns Movie Night Into a Quiet Cinema by the Sea
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Four Seasons Resort Bali at Jimbaran Bay is giving movie night a distinctly beachfront setting with the launch of Jimbaran Cinema, a “Quiet Cinema” experience at the resort’s secluded Coconut Grove. Running Sundays and Mondays from September 13 through November 9, the open-air screenings pair sunset drinks, relaxed beachfront dining and classic films with a headphone-based audio experience that leaves the sound of the waves undisturbed.

Guests settle into bean bags, sun beds or armchair sofas at 6 p.m. for a sunset drink before the film begins at 7:30 p.m. Using CineWav, the movie soundtrack is streamed directly to guests’ mobile phones through their own earphones, creating a more intimate viewing experience. Sunday screenings are geared toward families and friends with films including Mamma Mia! and The Greatest Showman, while Mondays take a more romantic turn with titles such as The Notebook. In-seat service continues throughout the film, with popcorn, soft drinks and juice included, alongside a menu of elevated cinema snacks such as lobster rolls, coconut crab nachos, Korean-style fried chicken and truffle parmesan fries.

The Curated Take

The cleverness of Jimbaran Cinema is that the technology is designed to make the setting quieter, not louder. By keeping the soundtrack in guests’ ears, the experience preserves the natural soundscape of Jimbaran Bay while transforming the beach into a private-feeling cinema beneath the stars. It is a simple idea, but one that feels particularly well suited to Bali, where the environment is as much a part of the evening as the movie itself.

item.title: Kandooma Maldives Reimagines the Island Experience Beyond the Rebrand
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
When Holiday Inn Resort Kandooma Maldives becomes Kandooma Maldives on October 1, the change will represent far more than a new name. The South Malé Atoll resort is using the transition to reshape its guest experience, with refreshed and new dining and leisure concepts, additional accommodation options, upgraded villas and a new approach to All-Inclusive built around the experiences travelers come to the Maldives to enjoy.

The resort is organizing its new identity around five signatures: Kandooma Blue, Kandooma Flow, Kandooma Table, Kandooma Social and Kandooma Ways, encompassing ocean experiences, movement and wellbeing, food, social connection and opportunities to discover Maldivian island life. Diving, surfing and watersports remain central, while the resort is expanding its land-based activities and offerings for families and teenagers. A new Kandooma Beach Club is also planned, alongside a phased refurbishment of villas and public spaces. Once the transformation is complete, the resort will offer 146 villas, including new two-bedroom accommodations.

The Curated Take

The more interesting part of Kandooma’s rebrand is its philosophy that All-Inclusive should be measured in memories rather than meals. By making activities such as scuba diving part of the proposition and building the brand around the island itself, Kandooma is positioning the resort as an experience to participate in rather than simply a place to stay. For a destination where many resorts can begin to blur together, that focus on what makes one particular island distinctive could be the more meaningful transformation.

item.title: China Moves Onto the Wish Lists of Younger Travelers
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
China may be poised for a bigger role in the young-traveler market. A 12-month poll of 13,256 INTRO Travel customers found that more than one in five named China among their top choices for a future trip, prompting the group tour operator to develop its first China program for travelers ages 18 to 40. The two proposed itineraries combine major cultural landmarks with destinations that have become increasingly visible on social media, including Zhangjiajie, Chengdu and Chongqing.

The 12-day China Express travels from Shanghai through Zhangjiajie, Chengdu, Xi’an, Luoyang and Dengfeng before reaching Beijing, while the 17-day China Adventure begins in Hong Kong and adds Yangshuo, Chongqing and Shanghai. Both include major draws such as the Great Wall, Terracotta Army and Forbidden City, with high-speed rail connecting much of the journey. Groups will be capped at 16, with the format designed to ease some of the practical challenges first-time visitors can face, from transportation and payments to navigating a country where independent travel can require more preparation.

The Curated Take

China has long had the cultural depth to appeal to adventurous travelers, but it has not carried the same easy familiarity among younger Western travelers as Thailand, Bali or Japan. That may be changing. Greater visa accessibility for some travelers, growing social-media visibility and the appeal of seeing somewhere that still feels less predictable could give China a new position in the young-traveler landscape. INTRO’s approach is particularly telling: rather than treating China as a complicated destination to conquer independently, it packages the logistical complexity into a social, fast-moving group journey.

item.title: Detroit to Host the Inaugural MICHELIN Guide American Great Lakes Ceremony
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Detroit will take center stage in the culinary world next spring when Michigan Central hosts the inaugural MICHELIN Guide American Great Lakes Ceremony on April 21. The event will bring together chefs and culinary leaders from across the region as the MICHELIN Guide prepares to unveil its first selections for the American Great Lakes, with restaurants potentially receiving MICHELIN Stars, Bib Gourmand distinctions or other Guide recognition. Attendance will be by invitation only, with chefs invited to discover their restaurants’ distinctions at the ceremony.

The choice of Detroit reflects the city’s growing profile as a destination shaped by culinary creativity, cultural depth and a distinct local identity. The ceremony also marks the arrival of the MICHELIN Guide’s American Great Lakes selection in 2027, expanding its North American footprint to another major culinary region. By rotating its annual ceremony among destinations, the Guide says it aims to spotlight the diversity of cuisines and the culinary talent emerging across its growing portfolio.

The Curated Take

For travelers, the significance goes beyond the ceremony itself. MICHELIN recognition can put an entire dining destination on the radar of food-focused travelers, and bringing the inaugural Great Lakes celebration to Detroit gives the city a particularly visible role in introducing the region’s culinary landscape to an international audience. The April ceremony could also offer an early glimpse at the restaurants likely to shape the Great Lakes dining conversation in the years ahead.

item.title: Four Seasons Kuda Huraa Opens a Private Island Dedicated to Naturopathic Wellness
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
At Four Seasons Resort Maldives at Kuda Huraa, wellness is moving beyond the traditional spa experience with the debut of ŪRJĀ Naturopathy Island, a dedicated wellness destination centered on naturopathic care, personalized guidance and sustainable wellbeing. Named for the Sanskrit word for vitality, ŪRJĀ combines naturopathic principles with scientific expertise, with programs designed around four core pathways: Rest & Rebalance, Cleanse, Nourish and Reconnect.

Reached by a traditional Maldivian dhoni from the resort’s main jetty, the island places wellness within a distinctly natural setting, with over-water treatment suites, open-air rituals and the surrounding ocean shaping the experience. Each journey begins with a naturopathic consultation, followed by individualized therapies, nutrition guidance and educational tools designed to help guests better understand their own wellbeing. Signature experiences include mud therapy, heliotherapy, sound healing, acupuncture and the Vagus Reset, while specialized programs address areas such as sleep, liver health and joint care. Yoga therapy is also offered as part of the program.

The Curated Take

ŪRJĀ is interesting because it treats a wellness retreat as an opportunity to learn, not simply unwind. The emphasis on consultation, education and practical habits gives the experience a more immersive dimension, while the private-island setting adds the kind of quiet and separation that can make meaningful restoration possible. For travelers increasingly looking for wellness experiences with a sense of purpose, the concept reflects a broader shift from the conventional spa escape toward more individualized approaches to wellbeing.

item.title: The Inn of The Five Graces Opens a Private Villa Inside One of Santa Fe’s Historic Homes
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Behind a weathered red gate in Santa Fe’s Barrio de Analco, The Inn of The Five Graces has unveiled Red Door, a private two-bedroom villa set within the historic Roque Tudesqui House. The approximately 2,000-square-foot residence offers guests the rare experience of staying inside a centuries-old adobe structure, with two private courtyards, a back deck, an expansive living room, dining room, kitchenette and richly appointed bedrooms. The house predates the Spanish colonial adobe era, with portions built using puddled adobe, an Indigenous construction technique that predates the introduction of Spanish-style adobe bricks.

Inside, Red Door reflects the distinctive design language of The Inn of The Five Graces, pairing historic architecture with rare antiques, custom textiles and intricate hand-laid mosaics collected from around the world. The villa’s secluded setting gives it the atmosphere of a private Santa Fe residence while retaining access to the inn’s hospitality and amenities. Adding another layer to the experience, the property’s celebrated wisteria, which cascades into purple blooms each June, is protected by a permanent preservation easement.

The Curated Take

Red Door is compelling precisely because the luxury here is inseparable from a sense of place. Rather than recreating Santa Fe’s history as décor, the villa places guests inside a building that has witnessed centuries of the city’s evolution. For travelers drawn to architecture, design and culturally layered stays, it offers something increasingly rare: the chance to experience Santa Fe not simply as a destination, but from within one of its historic homes.

item.title: Sa-Nga and Supattra Thai Dining Bring Regional Thai Flavors to One Intimate Dinner
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
At Centara Reserve Samui, Sa-Nga welcomed one of Koh Samui’s most celebrated Thai dining destinations, Supattra Thai Dining, for a one-night culinary collaboration on August 30. Known for its authentic Thai cuisine, locally sourced ingredients and deep appreciation for regional culinary traditions, Supattra joined Sa-Nga for an intimate seven-course dinner limited to just 18 guests.

The menu moved across Thailand’s diverse regional flavors, beginning with Sa-Nga’s Khao Yum Sa-Nga, followed by four dishes from Chef Supattra: Yum Pla, Nuea Mok, Gaeng Huaplee and Gaeng Puu. Sa-Nga closed the evening with Som Chun and Saku Lamyai. The collaboration brought together two culinary teams united by a shared approach to Thai gastronomy, balancing heritage, seasonality and craftsmanship with contemporary presentation.

The Curated Take

The appeal here is less about a special-event dinner and more about the opportunity to experience Thai cuisine through two distinct culinary perspectives. For travelers staying on Koh Samui, intimate collaborations like this offer a deeper introduction to the destination’s food culture, particularly when local chefs are given space to showcase the regional traditions and ingredients that shape their cooking.

item.title: Under the Full Moon, REVĪVŌ Bali Turns Wellness Into Ritual
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Each month, as the full moon rises over Bali, REVĪVŌ Wellness Resort Bali invites guests and the wider community to step away from the pace of everyday life with its Monthly Full Moon, Cacao & Sound Healing Ceremony. The recurring evening combines cacao, sound healing and mindful reflection in an intentionally unhurried ritual centered on the traditional symbolism of the full moon as a time of completion, release and renewal. Rather than filling the evening with activities, the experience creates space for participants to slow down, turn inward and reconnect with the present.

Held within the tranquil surroundings of the Nusa Dua wellness resort, the ceremony begins with cacao, described as a heart-opening ritual, before moving into immersive sound healing. Participants are encouraged to engage with the experience in their own way, whether seeking stillness, emotional release or simply a moment of deeper connection. The monthly gathering forms part of REVĪVŌ’s broader wellness calendar and offers a recurring opportunity to mark the transition between what has been and what comes next.

The Curated Take

There is something appealing about a wellness experience built around doing less. In a destination where itineraries can easily become packed with treatments, excursions and activities, REVĪVŌ’s full moon ceremony offers a deliberate pause. The ritual gives travelers a chance to experience Bali not through another scheduled activity, but through stillness, reflection and a connection to the rhythms of the natural world.

item.title: Meet Amelia, Boston Logan’s Holographic AI Concierge
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Navigating a busy airport may soon feel a little more like having a personal guide. Boston Logan International Airport has introduced Amelia, a life-size, hyper-realistic AI hologram designed to help passengers find gates, restaurants, shops, lounges and baggage claim through natural conversation. The pilot, launched by the Massachusetts Port Authority in partnership with Proto Hologram and Holomedia AI, combines a human-scale holographic presence with live mapping, airport information and real-time TSA wait times.

Amelia can communicate in up to 40 languages, with English, Spanish and French included in the initial service, and can connect travelers with a live customer service agent when human assistance is needed. Accessibility features include closed captioning, high-contrast displays, WCAG-compliant mapping and wheelchair-accessible positioning. The system is designed to remain available around the clock while helping airport staff focus on more complex passenger needs.

The Curated Take

The intriguing part of Amelia isn’t simply that she is a hologram. It is the attempt to make airport technology feel more intuitive and human at precisely the moment travelers tend to feel most disoriented. If passengers can ask a question naturally, see the route mapped in real time and still reach a human when necessary, the technology could make one of travel’s least glamorous rituals, getting through an airport, noticeably calmer.
